definitions.gloss: to load; to load up; to pack into
definitions.explanation: To load cargo, luggage, or goods into a vehicle, container, or ship.

examples.japanese: {荷物|にもつ}を{車|くるま}に{積|つ}み{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: I loaded the luggage into the car.

examples.japanese: トラックに{大量|たいりょう}の{段|だん}ボールを{積|つ}み{込|こ}む。
examples.english: To load a large number of cardboard boxes onto a truck.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{日|ひ}、{朝|あさ}から{家具|かぐ}をトラックに{積|つ}み{込|こ}む{作業|さぎょう}に{追|お}われた。
examples.english: On moving day, I was busy loading furniture onto the truck from early morning.

notes:
FORMATION:
A compound verb from {積|つ}む (to pile up, to load) + {込|こ}む (into). The こむ suffix adds the nuance of packing things into a confined space.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {荷物|にもつ}を{積|つ}み{込|こ}む (to load luggage)
- {車|くるま}に{積|つ}み{込|こ}む (to load into a car)
- トラックに{積|つ}み{込|こ}む (to load onto a truck)

CONTRAST:
- {荷|に}おろし / {荷下|におろ}し: unloading — the opposite action
